classification.difficultyReason: Construct differences from signed ordinate gaps, preserving the common domain and distinguishing intersections, finite endpoints and symmetry without supplied equations.

content.prompt: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$, graph $y=f(x)-g(x)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 24, upper-left figure in the 24–27 group.
spec.description: Unmarked Cartesian axes. Increasing blue straight line and decreasing orange straight line, each with arrows at both ends; equal and opposite ordinate offsets at the y-axis and a common intersection on the positive x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Preserve the schematic straight lines and their intersection. Coordinates in the drawing establish proportions only; no numerical scale, intercept value or equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.short:
An increasing straight line, steeper than $f$, crossing the $x$-axis where $f$ and $g$ intersect and crossing the $y$-axis below $f$.

Plot the signed vertical gap $f(x)-g(x)$.
answer.worked: Subtract the ordinate of $g$ from that of $f$ at each $x$. To the left of their intersection, $f<g$, so the difference is negative. At the intersection it is zero; to the right it is positive. The gap increases at a constant rate, producing the steeper straight line shown.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 24; answer-book PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 24.
spec.description: Complete difference graph with dashed component lines and a solid steeper increasing line.
spec.mathematics: The solid line represents the signed ordinate difference in the same schematic coordinate frame as the supplied graph. Its zero coincides with the component intersection.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 25, upper-right figure in the 24–27 group.
spec.description: Matching upper semicircular arcs: blue f has endpoints at height 2; orange g has endpoints at height −1 and its highest point at the origin. Dashed vertical guides align corresponding endpoints.
spec.mathematics: The arcs have identical shapes and horizontal extent. Their ordinate difference is 3 throughout their common closed domain. Horizontal drawing coordinates are unlabelled and do not supply endpoint abscissae.
spec.answerVisibility: Only component arcs, the supplied ordinate labels and endpoint guides are visible.

answer.short: The horizontal segment $y=3$, including both endpoints, over the common domain of the two arcs.
answer.worked: The matching arcs are vertically separated by $2-(-1)=3$. Hence $f(x)-g(x)=3$ at every common $x$-value. Draw a horizontal segment at height 3 with closed endpoints aligned with the supplied arc endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 25; answer-book PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 25.
spec.description: Horizontal segment at height 3 with two closed endpoints; component arcs are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Constant ordinate difference 3 on the common closed domain. Endpoint horizontal values remain unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed graph and the result label 3 are solution-only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 26, lower-left figure in the 24–27 group.
spec.description: Blue increasing concave-down curve beginning on the negative x-axis; orange reflected decreasing curve ending on the positive x-axis. They share a positive y-intercept and have arrows on their unbounded ends.
spec.mathematics: Schematic reflected curves with finite inner endpoints. The unlabelled rendering frame models their visible shape only; no curve equation or numerical coordinate is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied component curves are visible.

answer.short:
An increasing S-shaped curve through the origin, negative on the left and positive on the right, with closed endpoints over the common domain.

Use the signed vertical gaps between the supplied curves.
answer.worked: Use only the horizontal interval where both curves exist. On its left half, $f<g$, so the difference is negative. At $x=0$, the ordinates agree, giving zero. On its right half, $f>g$, so the difference is positive. The reflected component curves give a difference graph symmetric about the origin, steep near both finite endpoints. At the left endpoint the difference is $-g(x)$; at the right endpoint it is $f(x)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 26; answer-book PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 26.
spec.description: Increasing S-shaped difference curve through the origin, with finite closed endpoints; dashed component curves provide context.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative graph on the common interval. Endpoints lie at the negative right-component ordinate on the left and the positive left-component ordinate on the right. No equations or numerical endpoint values are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: The difference curve and its endpoint markers are solution-only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 27, lower-right figure in the 24–27 group.
spec.description: Blue upward-opening parabola with arrows at both upper ends; orange upper semicircle ending on the x-axis. Both are symmetric about the y-axis, and the parabola vertex coincides with the semicircle maximum.
spec.mathematics: Preserve the common point, symmetry and finite semicircle domain. Drawing coordinates establish proportions only; no radius, endpoint coordinate or parabola equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied component graphs are visible.

answer.short:
A curve symmetric about the $y$-axis, with minimum at the origin and two rising branches ending at closed endpoints above the $x$-axis.

Plot the positive vertical gaps on the semicircle's domain.
answer.worked: Restrict the sketch to the domain of the semicircle. At $x=0$, $f=g$, so the difference is zero. On either side, $f>g$, and their vertical gap increases towards the endpoints. Both component graphs are symmetric about the $y$-axis, so the difference is symmetric too. At each endpoint $g=0$, so the difference has the ordinate of $f$ there. Include both endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 27; answer-book PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 27.
spec.description: Symmetric difference curve with minimum at the origin and two closed endpoints; component graphs are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative difference on the semicircle's closed domain. It is zero only at the shared central point and positive elsewhere; endpoint ordinates agree with f because g is zero.
spec.answerVisibility: The completed difference and endpoint markers are solution-only.
